problem:
Consider the following trigonometric  equation:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡2x=-2
$$

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as 

$$
x=a+\pi n,\,x=\frac{11\pi }{12}+\pi n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation:

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡(5x)=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}
$$

The general solution of this equation is

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{2\pi n}{5},\,x=a+\frac{2\pi n}{5},
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Which of the following could be the value of $a?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, note that the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
5x=\frac{5\pi }{6}+2\pi n,\,5x=\frac{7\pi }{6}+2\pi n.
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & =\frac{5\pi }{6}+2\pi n, & \,5x & =\frac{7\pi }{6}+2\pi n \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{2\pi n}{5}, & \,x & =\frac{7\pi }{30}+\frac{2\pi n}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have that $a=\frac{7\pi }{30}.$
